key_insight: Nonuniform evaporation creates coupled thermal and solutal Marangoni forces that can make sessile binary-mixture droplets attract, repel, or chase one another.
engineering_relevance: The study helps predict and control droplet motion in coating, printing, and microfluidic evaporation processes where composition-dependent interactions matter.
method: Lubrication-theory model for thin evaporating binary droplets
Finite-element solution of coupled evolution equations for droplet profiles and vapor diffusion
Parameter study of pure and binary droplet pairs with experiments on water–morpholine droplets
evidence_signal: The model’s predicted attraction, repulsion, and chasing behaviors were checked against experiments using water–morpholine binary-mixture droplets.
watch_item: The approach is built for thin sessile droplets under lubrication assumptions, so accuracy may drop for thicker drops or strongly inertial flows.
paper_title: Translation dynamics of evaporating sessile binary-mixture droplet populations
